thread:
Maya Chen: Hey infra — we're hitting Target registration failures when provisioning new inference nodes in eu-west-2 (redwood-dedicated-02). Errors look like: "TooManyTargets: Cannot register more targets, status code 400". Suspect we've hit interface endpoint / NLB target limits. Can infra request quota increases?
Luke Patel: On it. Can you paste the exact error snippet + the AWS account and VPC? Also confirm whether this is NLB target registrations or ENI/interface endpoint count.
Maya Chen: Log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T16:22:11Z ERROR TargetRegistration failed: TooManyTargets: Cannot register more targets for targetgroup arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-2:987654321012:targetgroup/tg-infer-01/abcd1234
Current counts: interface endpoints (com.amazonaws.ec2) = 52 / 50 (soft-limit), NLB targets ~480 / 500 in eu-west-2 across AZs. Cluster: redwood-dedicated-02, VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d, AWS account: 987654321012
```
infra-buddy-bot: Quota dashboard snapshot: eu-west-2 Interface Endpoints per VPC: 52/50; Network LB targets per target group: 480/500; Account-wide NLB targets: 4,800/5,000.
Amanda R.: Short-term mitigation: can we stagger the daemonset rollout or reuse existing target groups to avoid burst registration? We should also gate canary to 10 pods at a time while infra sorts quotas.
Ron Gomez: Note that ALB wouldn't satisfy the static IP requirement for customer-facing endpoints. NLB is required for preserving client source IPs and static mappings. For immediate unblock, stagger rollouts + increase retry backoff in the registration controller.
Luke Patel: I'll open an AWS support case now. Proposed quota requests:
- Interface Endpoints per VPC (eu-west-2): 200
- NLB per-target-group target limit (or registration cap): raise to 2,000
- NLB target registration rate / concurrency increase to 2,000
Justification: Dedicated inference fleet will scale to ~3k simultaneous targets during peak rollout for multi-AZ inference pools. Contact: infra-ops@redwood.ai. ETA to open case: 10m.
Maya Chen: Please include the error sample and the log link: https://internal-logs/cluster/redwood-dedicated-02/attach-fail. Also tag account manager if needed.
Amanda R.: I'll implement rollout throttling and a preflight check that queries current interface endpoint count and delays pod creation if >40.
Luke Patel: AWS case created: case-1234567890 (service: vpc-endpoints & elb). Status: Pending - needs business justification. I've added the scale matrix and contact details.
infra-buddy-bot: Ticket update: Awaiting AWS quota team review. Suggested explanations accepted; ETA asked for expected sustained targets per day.
Maya Chen: After the bump, can we add an alert: quota usage > 70% in the infra dashboard (per-region) + auto-hold on new rollouts? Would prevent surprise.
Ron Gomez: I'll author a short RFC to reduce registration churn: consolidate high-churn pods into fewer target groups and add connection draining to avoid thrash. Drafting now.
Amanda R.: FYI I'm also monitoring ap-southeast-1 for the same pattern — might be regional. Will post if we see hits.
Luke Patel: Will update this thread with AWS case progress and final quota numbers. If anyone sees more errors in the meantime, ping me directly. Thanks all :thumbsup:
